$\mathrm{emf}=-\frac{d \phi}{d t}$

& =6 t^2+8 t+2
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
	ext{At } t & =5 s \\
e & =6(5)^2+8(5)+2 \\
& =192 \mathrm{~V}
\end{aligned}$

$= \dfrac{{π}^{2}B^{2}r^{4}{ω}^{2}}{4R} \cdot \dfrac{1}{2}$~ & $\left[∵ \overset{¯}{{sin}^{2}\omegat} = \dfrac{1}{2}\right]$

If the total charge flown through the coil is \(75 \times10^{-3} $\mathrm{C}\) and the total resistance of wire and galvanometer is \(0.3 \Omega\), then the magnitude of the magnetic field is
questions.solution:

number of turns in the coil, N=30\) turns
area of $the coil, \(A=2.5 \mathrm{ cm}^2=2.5 \times10^{-4} \mathrm{ m}^2\)
total charge flowing through$ the $coil,
\(Q_{\text{Net }}=7.5 \times10^{-3} \mathrm{C}\)
and total resistance of wire and galvanometer,
\(R=0.3 \Omega\)
We know that,
\(\text{ net charge, }Q_{n e t}=\frac{\text{ flux in the coil }}{\text{ net Resistance }}\)
\(\therefore \quad Q_{\text{net }}=\frac{\phi}{R}\)...(i)
We know that, flux \(\phi=\) magnetic field \(\times\) area
\(\times\) number of turns in the coil
or \(\phi=B N A\)...(ii)
Now, from Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
\(\therefore \quad Q_{\text{Net }}=\frac{B N A}{R}\)
Putting the given values, we get
\begin{aligned}7.5 \times10^{-3} & =\frac{B \times 30 \times\left(2.5 \times 10^{-4}\right)}{0.3}\\
7.5 \times10^{-3} & =\frac{B \times 7.5 \times 10^{-3}}{0.3}\\
B & =0.3 \mathrm{ T}
\end{aligned}$
Hence, the magnitude of the magnetic field, \(B=0.3 \mathrm{ T}\).

$⇒ R^{2} + $\dfrac{r2}{2} =$ r^{2}$

$⇒ r = R\sqrt{2}$

As shown in figure, the two parallel conducting rails, in a horizontal plane, are connected at one end by an inductor of inductance$L$. A slider (metallic) of mass $m$, is imparted a velocity ${v}_{0}_{,} upon the rails, as shown in figure. The period of oscillation of the conducting rod is

$
questions.solution:
From energy conservation (there are no dissipative forces)-

$E = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}LI^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{m}{2} \times 2v\dfrac{dv}{dt} + \dfrac{L}{2} \times 2I\dfrac{dI}{dt} = 0$

$mv\dfrac{dv}{dt} = - IL\dfrac{dI}{dt}$

The emf induced in an inductor is

$E = L\dfrac{dI}{dt} = Blv$

$⇒ L\dfrac{dI}{dt} = Bl\dfrac{dx}{dt} ⇒ LdI = Bldx ⇒ I = \dfrac{Bl}{L}x$

The force acting on a current-carrying conductor is

$m\dfrac{dv}{dt} = - IBl$

$⇒ \dfrac{dv}{dt} = - \dfrac{IBl}{m}$

Substituting the value of $I$ we get

$\dfrac{dv}{dt} = - \left(\dfrac{Bl}{L}x\right)\dfrac{Bl}{m} ⇒ a = - \left(\dfrac{B^{2}l^{2}}{mL}\right)x$

We got acceleration in the form of

$a = - {ω}^{2}x$

this implies that the motion is& SHM, with angular frequency

$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{B^{2}l^{2}}{mL}}$

The time period of motion is
$⇒ T = 2\pi\dfrac{\sqrt{mL}}{Bl}$
